'''Andre Tyler Iguodala''' ({{IPAc-en|ɪ|ɡ|w|ə|ˈ|d|ɑː|l|ə}} {{respell|ig|wə|DAH|lə}}; born January 28, 1984)<ref>{{cite web|title=Andre Iguodala Stats|url=https://www.basketball-reference.com/players/i/iguodan01.html|access-date=2020-11-05|website=Basketball-Reference.com|language=en}}</ref> is an American former professional [[basketball]] player who played for 19 seasons in the [[National Basketball Association]] (NBA). A [[swingman]], he was an [[NBA All-Star Game|NBA All-Star]] in 2012 and was named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Team]] twice. Iguodala won four [[NBA championship]]s with the [[Golden State Warriors]] and was named the [[NBA Finals Most Valuable Player]] (FMVP) in 2015. He was also a member of the [[United States men's national basketball team|U.S. national team]] at the [[2010 FIBA World Championship]] and [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics|2012 Summer Olympics]], winning the gold medal both times.<ref>{{Cite web|title=Andre Iguodala {{!}} NBA.com|url=https://www.nba.com/player/2738/andre_iguodala|access-date=2020-11-05|website=NBA}}</ref>

Iguodala played [[college basketball]] with the [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona Wildcats]]. After earning first-team [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] honors in the Pac-10 (known now as the [[Pac-12 Conference men's basketball|Pac-12]]) as a sophomore in 2004, he was selected in the [[2004 NBA draft]] with the ninth overall pick by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. Iguodala played for Philadelphia until the summer of 2012 when he joined the [[Denver Nuggets]] in a four-team trade. He was acquired by Golden State in 2013. In 2014–15, Iguodala became a [[reserve (sport)|reserve]] for the first time in his career, but played a major role. He captured the Finals MVP after returning to the [[starting lineup]] in the middle of the championship series. After three championships and five trips to the Finals with the Warriors, Iguodala had a two-year stint with the [[Miami Heat]], with whom he reached his sixth straight Finals in 2020. Iguodala returned to Golden State in 2021 and won his fourth NBA championship that season. He spent another season with the Warriors before retiring from playing in 2023.

From February 2019 to February 2023, Iguodala served as vice-president of the [[National Basketball Players Association]] (NBPA). On November 9, 2023, the NBPA executive committee appointed him as acting executive director.<ref name=":2">{{cite web |title=NBPA ANNOUNCES ANDRE IGUODALA AS ACTING EXECUTIVE Director |url=https://nbpa.com/news/nbpa-announces-andre-iguodala-as-acting-executive-director |website=NBPA.com |access-date=19 December 2023 |language=en}}</ref>

==Early life==
Iguodala was born in [[Springfield, Illinois]], the son of Linda Shanklin. His older brother, Frank, played for [[Lake Land College]] in [[Mattoon, Illinois]], and [[Dayton Flyers men's basketball|Dayton]].<ref>[http://www.nba.com/playerfile/andre_iguodala/bio.html NBA.com player profile] {{Webarchive|url=https://web.archive.org/web/20091230021158/http://www.nba.com/playerfile/andre_iguodala/bio.html |date=December 30, 2009}}.</ref> His mother is [[African American]] and his father is [[Nigerians|Nigerian]].<ref name="iguodala1">{{cite web|url=http://iguodala9.com/wp/?page_id=99 |title=iguodala9.com |publisher=iguodala9.com |access-date=August 4, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120326194950/http://iguodala9.com/wp/?page_id=99 |archive-date=March 26, 2012}}</ref> Growing up, Iguodala was a [[Chicago Bulls]] fan, and cites [[Michael Jordan]] as the player he looked up to the most.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.mindofai9.com/history|title=Andre Iguodala - Mind of AI9|website=www.mindofai9.com|access-date=March 27, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20171217140759/http://mindofai9.com/history|archive-date=December 17, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref>

Iguodala attended [[Lanphier High School]] in Springfield, Illinois, which had produced such notable athletes as baseball Hall of Famer [[Robin Roberts (baseball)|Robin Roberts]] and NBA guard [[Kevin Gamble]]. Iguodala did well there both academically and athletically, winning All-Conference academic honors, making the National Honor Roll, being named ''[[The State Journal-Register|State Journal-Register]]'' Student-Athlete of the Week several times,<ref name="arizonawildcats1">{{cite web|url=http://www.arizonawildcats.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/iguodala_andre00.html |title=Player Bio: Andre Iguodala – University of Arizona Wildcats Official Athletic Site |publisher=Arizonawildcats.com |access-date=August 4, 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120608061506/http://www.arizonawildcats.com/sports/m-baskbl/mtt/iguodala_andre00.html |archive-date=June 8, 2012}}</ref> and earning three letters in track for the high jump.<ref name="iguodala1" /><ref>{{ cite web |url=http://visuals.sj-r.com/andre-iguodalas-springfield-roots-june-17-2015/ |title=Andre Iguodala's Springfield's roots |date=June 17, 2015 |access-date=June 3, 2016 |publisher=The Visual Journal |website=visuals.sj-r.com | archive-date=August 13, 2016 | archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20160813200109/http://visuals.sj-r.com/andre-iguodalas-springfield-roots-june-17-2015/ | url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://articles.philly.com/2009-04-12/sports/24985039_1_flashes-glimpses-boys-girls-club |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110625161610/http://articles.philly.com/2009-04-12/sports/24985039_1_flashes-glimpses-boys-girls-club |url-status=dead |archive-date=June 25, 2011 |title=Looking into the life of the Sixers' Andre Iguodala |date=April 12, 2009 |access-date=June 3, 2016 |first=Kate |last=Fagan |website=philly.com}}</ref> As a senior in 2002, Iguodala led Lanphier's basketball team to a runner-up finish at the Illinois High School Association Class AA state tournament. That season, he averaged 23.5 points, 7.8 rebounds and 4.1 assists per game. Iguodala was named ''[[Chicago Sun-Times]]'' Player of the Year as well as a second-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] and Nike All-American. He was also a finalist for the [[Illinois Mr. Basketball]] award, which was won by [[Dee Brown (basketball, born 1984)|Dee Brown]]. Iguodala's Lanphier jersey is now retired.

During the summer of 2000, Iguodala captured the attention of coaches around the nation by hitting a game-winning [[buzzer-beater]] to give his team the 17-and-under [[Amateur Athletic Union|AAU]] national title and being named the tournament MVP. In 2002, Iguodala played in the [[Jordan Brand Classic]] in Washington, D.C. In 22 minutes of play, he put up six points on 3–6 shooting, five rebounds, two assists, three steals, and a block. Iguodala played AAU basketball under Larry Butler and the Illinois Warriors, the team that has featured other professional players such as [[Dwyane Wade]] and [[Quentin Richardson]], and [[Duke University|Duke]] head coach [[Jon Scheyer]].

Considered a four-star recruit by [[Scout.com]], Iguodala was listed as the No. 6 [[small forward]] and the No. 26 player in the nation in 2002.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://scouthoops.scout.com/player/10790n-andre-iguodala|title=Andre Iguodala Recruiting Profile|website=scout.com|access-date=March 27, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150402123753/http://scouthoops.scout.com/player/10790n-andre-iguodala|archive-date=April 2, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref>

==College career==
Iguodala initially signed a [[National Letter of Intent]] to play at [[Arkansas Razorbacks men's basketball|Arkansas]]. He had narrowed down his list of desired schools to two: [[Kansas Jayhawks men's basketball|Kansas]] or Arkansas. Iguodala was enticed by Arkansas's 1–3 system, which would have allowed Iguodala to run the point occasionally. Iguodala visited the Arkansas campus and was impressed by their [[Bud Walton Arena|large gymnasium]] and the number of fans at a practice while there with his mother and father.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://highschoolelite.com/news/11+5.html |title=Operating on the Hardwood- Andre Iguodala to Arkansas |publisher=Highschoolelite.com |access-date=August 4, 2012}}</ref> After their coach, [[Nolan Richardson]], was fired that year (2002), Iguodala decided to attend [[Arizona Wildcats men's basketball|Arizona]] instead. At Arizona, he joined future NBA players [[Channing Frye]], [[Luke Walton]], [[Mustafa Shakur]], [[Salim Stoudamire]] and [[Hassan Adams]]. One of the determining factors for Iguodala was the commitment of Hassan Adams, whom Iguodala had played with in the Jordan Brand Classic in high school. Many colleges regarded Iguodala as a track star turned basketball player, but teammate Luke Walton said, "He is going to be one of the best players to ever come out of Arizona by the time he is done here." Iguodala was named to the Pac-10 All-Freshmen team for 2002–03. In his freshman year, Iguodala quickly established himself as one of the best all-around players on the team, ranking in the top 5 for his team in just about every major category.<ref name="iguodala1"/>

As a sophomore in 2003–04, Iguodala was named team MVP after leading his team in rebounds, assists and steals. He also made the [[List of All-Pac-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-10 First Team]] and was named Honorable Mention All-America by ''[[The Associated Press]]''. Iguodala collected three [[triple-double]]s that season, joining [[Jason Kidd]] as the only two players in [[Pacific-10 Conference|Pac-10]] history to post two or more triple-doubles in a season. During his career at Arizona, the Wildcats made it to the NCAA Tournament both seasons. In his freshman year, the Wildcats were defeated in the Elite Eight by Kansas. In his sophomore year, Arizona was defeated in the first round by [[Seton Hall Pirates men's basketball|Seton Hall]]. After posting career totals of 594 points (9.6 ppg), 409 rebounds (6.6 rpg) and 95 steals (1.53 spg) in 62 games (34 starts), Iguodala left to enter the NBA draft. At Arizona, Iguodala planned to major in education.<ref name="iguodala1"/> After the season, he signed with agent [[Rob Pelinka]], co-founder of the Landmark Sports Agency, who had represented NBA All-Stars such as [[Kobe Bryant]], [[Carlos Boozer]], and [[Gerald Wallace]].<ref name="New Pippen"/><ref name=":0">{{Cite news|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/20750344/andre-iguodala-was-verge-leaving-golden-state-warriors|title=Inside the free-agency frenzy that almost cost the Warriors a Finals MVP|work=ESPN.com|access-date=September 22, 2017}}</ref>

==Professional career==

===Philadelphia 76ers (2004–2012)===
[[Image:Andreigoudala1.JPG|thumb|right|Iguodala warming up prior to a game for the 76ers]]

====2004–05 season: Rookie season====
Iguodala was selected 9th overall in the [[2004 NBA draft]] by the [[Philadelphia 76ers]]. When Iguodala was selected, ESPN personality [[Dick Vitale]] commented that it was a mistake for the Sixers to take him, saying: "Iguodala was a [27 percent] shooter from the college three-point line. He's not going to be able to play."<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/dickvitale/vcolumn040420draftmistakes.html|title=Dick Vitale - Some declaring for draft are making a mistake|website=ESPN|access-date=March 27, 2018}}</ref> Iguodala used this as motivation in what proved to be a very productive rookie [[2004–05 NBA season|season]].<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_km4470/is_200703/ai_n18702953|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20090204111822/http://findarticles.com/p/articles/mi_km4470/is_200703/ai_n18702953|url-status=usurped|archive-date=February 4, 2009|work=Philadelphia Daily News|date=March 2007|title=Turns out, it was Vitale's mistake|access-date=March 27, 2018}}</ref> He was thrust into the starting lineup immediately and was the only 76er to play and start all 82 regular-season games plus five playoff games, becoming a favorite target of [[Allen Iverson]] in the process, often connecting on highlight-reel dunks on passes or alley-oops from Iverson. Iguodala proved his versatility, as Iguodala was the only rookie and 76er to record a [[triple-double]] that season, doing it against the defending champion [[Detroit Pistons]]. In that game, he scored 10 points, caught 10 rebounds and dished out 10 assists. During the season, Iguodala averaged 9.0 points, 5.7 rebounds, 3 assists, 1.7 steals, and 32.8 minutes per game. His efforts were rewarded when he was named to the All-Rookie First Team and started on the rookie team during the Rookie Challenge portion of [[National Basketball Association All-Star Game|All-Star Weekend]].<ref>{{cite web|first=Matt|last=Wong|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/allstar2006/news/story?id=2335818 |title=Robinson wins dunkfest amid controversy |publisher= ESPN |date=February 21, 2006 |access-date=August 4, 2012}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url= https://www.sfgate.com/sports/article/Robinson-rises-above-Slam-Dunk-competition-2522810.php|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20110916222740/http://www.sfgate.com/cgi-bin/article.cgi?f=%2Fchronicle%2Farchive%2F2006%2F02%2F19%2FSPG3NHBG141.DTL|url-status=live|title=Robinson rises above Slam-Dunk competition|first=Janny|last=Hu|date=February 19, 2006|archive-date=September 16, 2011|website=SFGate|access-date=January 18, 2022}}</ref> Iguodala finished fourth in voting for [[NBA Rookie of the Year Award|NBA Rookie of the Year]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/hornets/news/okafor_roy_050504.html|title=Emeka Okafor Named 2004-05 NBA got milk? Rookie Of The Year|website=NBA|access-date=March 27, 2018}}</ref>

[[Image:Andre dunks.jpg|thumb|left|Iguodala competed in the [[2006 NBA All-Star Game#Sprite Rising Stars Slam Dunk Contest|2006 Slam Dunk Contest]].]]

====2005–06 season: Sophomore season====
Already a fixture in the 76ers' starting rotation, Iguodala was the only Sixer to play in and start all 82 games in his second season. On February 17, 2006, at the [[2006 NBA All-Star Game#T-Mobile Rookie Challenge|Rookie Challenge]], Iguodala won MVP honors for his 30-point performance in the Sophomores win.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://usatoday30.usatoday.com/sports/basketball/allstar/2006-02-17-rookie-challenge_x.htm|title=Iguodala powers sophomores in Rookie Challenge|website=USA Today|access-date=March 27, 2018}}</ref> The next day, he participated in the [[Slam Dunk Contest]]. Iguodala's first dunk was a simple windmill. Next, he received a pass from [[Allen Iverson]] off the back side of the backboard, leapt beneath the board, and reverse dunked on the other side, earning a perfect score of 50 points. In the final round, Iguodala did a behind-the-back dunk and followed with a reverse. However, in a controversial decision,<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/allstar2006/news/story?id=2335818|title=Robinson, not Iguodala, wins dunkfest amid controversy|date=February 19, 2006|website=ESPN.com|access-date=March 27, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.ign.com/articles/2006/11/08/andre-iguodala-interview|title=Andre Iguodala Interview|first=Jon|last=Robinson|date=November 8, 2006|website=ign.com|access-date=March 27, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.csnphilly.com/andre-iguodala-finally-speaks-being-robbed-2006-dunk-contest-nate-robinson-because-manny-pacquiao|title=Andre Iguodala Finally Speaks On Being Robbed of 2006 Dunk Contest By Nate Robinson (Because Of Manny Pacquiao)|date=June 10, 2012|website=CSN Philadelphia|access-date=March 27, 2018}}</ref> the award was given to [[Nate Robinson]]<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/allstar2006/rookie_challenge/recap.html |title=Iguodala Shines as Sophs Top Rookies |work=NBA.com |access-date=August 4, 2012}}</ref> (who had missed 14 straight dunk attempts before succeeding on his last).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.libertyballers.com/2015/2/12/8022521/andre-iguodala-2006-slam-dunk-contest-nate-robinson-oral-history|title=He Got (Nate) Robbed: The Oral History of the 2006 NBA Dunk Contest|website=Liberty Ballers|date=February 12, 2015|access-date=March 27, 2018}}</ref> Iguodala averaged 12.3 points and 5.9 rebounds on the season.

====2006–07 season: Leadership role====
After [[Allen Iverson]] was traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] and [[Chris Webber]] was released, Iguodala emerged as a team leader on the 76ers. At the time of Webber's release, the 76ers were 9–26 (Iverson only played 15 games before he was traded). Averaging 40.3 minutes per game during a late-season run, he paced the team to a 26–21 finish, just shy of the #8-seed in the Eastern Conference playoffs, albeit a record padded by other teams "tanking" to secure a higher draft pick.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://hoopsanalyst.com/blog/?p=362 |title=Philly Phlying: Refusing to Tank? |publisher=Hoops Analyst |date=March 25, 2008 |access-date=August 4, 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120410144544/http://hoopsanalyst.com/blog/?p=362 |archive-date=April 10, 2012 |url-status=dead}}</ref> Iguodala went on to finish the season with averages of 18.2 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 5.7 assists, combined tallies matched or bettered only by [[LeBron James]], [[Kobe Bryant]], and [[Tracy McGrady]].

====2007–08 season: Career high in scoring====
Iguodala got off to a slow start to the season, even to a point where he was leading the league in turnovers. Iguodala began to step up his game as the season went on, leading Philadelphia to a playoff berth. The 76ers finished the season at 40–42, winning 22 of their last 29 games and earning a playoff spot with a victory over the [[Atlanta Hawks]] on April 4. Iguodala averaged a career-high 19.9 points, 5.4 rebounds, and 4.8 assists per game through the 82 games. Philadelphia was set to face the No. 2 seed [[Detroit Pistons|Detroit]]. In the playoffs, the 76ers lost in the first round to the Pistons in six games despite a 2–1 lead. Iguodala had a poor postseason series, averaging 13 points per game.

====2008–09 season: Leading the NBA in minutes====
[[Image:Andre Iguodala over Mikki Moore.jpg|thumb|Iguodala pulls up for a jumper while being defended by [[Mikki Moore]].]]
On August 17, 2008, Iguodala signed a six-year, $80 million contract extension with the 76ers.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/news/story?id=3539834 |title=Iguodala signs reported six-year, $80 million deal with 76ers|publisher= ESPN |date=August 17, 2008 |access-date=January 18, 2023}}</ref> The contract had $5 million in bonuses and a player option for the sixth year.

Early on in the year, Iguodala was on a Sixers team with high expectations after signing All-Star forward [[Elton Brand]] and seeing the success of forward [[Thaddeus Young]], whom they drafted with their lottery pick the prior year. Iguodala developed into more of a primary player in the 2008–09 season, becoming more active as a facilitator on the offensive end of the floor. Early into the season, Philadelphia was struggling, which led to the departure of head coach [[Maurice Cheeks]]. The 76ers played much better basketball under interim head coach [[Tony DiLeo]]. In his last year with co-captain and veteran point guard [[Andre Miller]], Iguodala helped lead the 76ers to another playoff berth, finishing the season with a 41–41 season record and as the #6-seed in the Eastern Conference. In the playoffs the 76ers were set to face the third seed [[Orlando Magic]]. In Game 1, Orlando had an 18-point lead in the fourth quarter, but Philadelphia made an amazing comeback led by Iguodala, eventually scoring a step-back, fadeaway jumper in the face of [[Hedo Türkoğlu]] with 2.2 seconds remaining to give the 76ers the win. The 76ers eventually lost to the Magic in six games, failing to reach the second round. Iguodala had averaged 18.8 points, 5.7 rebounds, and 5.3 assists per game through 82 regular-season games.

====2009–10 season: Reunion with Allen Iverson====
In the preseason, Philadelphia drafted point guard [[Jrue Holiday]] out of [[UCLA]] to take over the void left at point guard after the departure of veteran point guard [[Andre Miller]], who had joined the [[Portland Trail Blazers]]. The Sixers hired coach [[Eddie Jordan (basketball)|Eddie Jordan]] to take over for [[Tony DiLeo]]. Iguodala averaged career-highs in rebounds, assists, and blocks, and a career-low in personal fouls. He finished the season averaging 17.1 points, 6.5 rebounds, 5.8 assists, and 1.7 steals. However, the 76ers were a big disappointment, going only 27–55 during the regular season and missing the playoffs after two straight playoff berths. During the season, the 76ers brought Iguodala's old friend [[Allen Iverson]] back in what would be his final season in the NBA before going to play overseas for [[Beşiktaş Cola Turka|Beşiktaş]].

====2010–11 season: All-Defensive Second Team====
Coming into the [[2010–11 NBA season]], the 76ers were expected to rebound from their poor season. They fired head coach [[Eddie Jordan (basketball)|Eddie Jordan]] and brought in [[Doug Collins (basketball)|Doug Collins]]. Philadelphia also traded veteran big man [[Samuel Dalembert]] to the [[Sacramento Kings]] for a younger center [[Spencer Hawes]]; the 76ers also acquired [[Andrés Nocioni]] in the deal. With the second overall pick in the draft, the Sixers made a big splash by drafting [[Evan Turner]]. Philadelphia started the season poorly but were one of the best teams down the stretch. During the season, Iguodala was hampered by an Achilles injury, leading to career lows in games played and started, field-goal percentage, free-throw percentage, and steals per game as the 76ers finished with a 41–41 record. However, Iguodala also had his career-best season in assists with 6.3 assists per game and helped the 76ers make the playoffs with the #7-seed in the Eastern Conference. During the year, Iguodala was the subject of multiple trade rumors that had him being traded to either the [[Golden State Warriors]], [[Los Angeles Clippers]] or [[Los Angeles Lakers]]. In the playoffs, Iguodala had the assignment of guarding James and [[Dwyane Wade]] in the first round. The 76ers were eventually defeated by the [[Miami Heat]] in five games. For his defensive efforts throughout the season, Iguodala was named to the [[NBA All-Defensive Team|NBA All-Defensive Team Second Team]], though his coaches and teammates lobbied for him to make the First Team. Iguodala showed his versatility during the season posting up a career-high in triple-doubles and was second behind James for most triple-doubles during the 2010–11 season.

====2011–12 season: All-Star selection====
During the [[2011 NBA lockout]], Iguodala had a week-long internship with [[Merrill Lynch]].<ref name=Merrill>{{cite news|last=Spears|first=Marc J.|title=Iguodala gets lesson in money game|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/iguodala-gets-lesson-money-game-201900840--nba.html|access-date=December 11, 2013|newspaper=Yahoo|date=September 29, 2011}}</ref>

On his 28th birthday, Iguodala recorded a 10-point, 10-rebound, 10-assist triple-double effort in a 95–74 victory over the Pistons. Later that season, he was selected to [[2012 NBA All-Star Game|his first All-Star Game]] as a reserve. Iguodala's scoring average was the lowest of all the 24 All-Stars, but he was rewarded for being the best player on the 76ers, who were leading the [[Atlantic Division (NBA)|Atlantic Division]]. Collins called Iguodala a "stat-sheet stuffer."<ref>{{cite news|last=Mitchell |first=John N. |title=Sixers' Iguodala is an NBA all-star |date=February 26, 2012 |newspaper=The Inquirer |url=http://articles.philly.com/2012-02-26/sports/31101513_1_sixers-iguodala-sixers-coach-doug-collins-andre-iguodala |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150411233816/http://articles.philly.com/2012-02-26/sports/31101513_1_sixers-iguodala-sixers-coach-doug-collins-andre-iguodala |archive-date=April 11, 2015 |url-status=dead}}</ref> At the end of the 2011–12 NBA season, Iguodala averaged 12.4 points, 6.1 rebounds, 5.5 assists, and 1.7 steals. He helped the 76ers clinch the final seed in the playoffs. In Game 6 of the first-round playoff series against the [[Chicago Bulls]], he made two free throws with 2.2 seconds left to win the game and help the 76ers upset the Bulls en route to the franchise's first playoff series win since 2003. This was also the fifth time in NBA history that a #8-seed defeated a #1-seed in the opening round of the playoffs. The 76ers were eventually eliminated by the [[Boston Celtics]] in a thrilling seven games in the Conference Semifinals.

===Denver Nuggets (2012–2013)===
[[File:Lakers vs Nuggets 2013-01-06 (6).JPG|thumb|right|Iguodala as a member of the Denver Nuggets]]
On August 10, 2012, Iguodala was traded to the [[Denver Nuggets]] in a series of trades also involving the Sixers, [[Los Angeles Lakers]], and [[Orlando Magic]]. Other players involved in the deal included All-Stars [[Andrew Bynum]] and [[Dwight Howard]]. The trade was completed just before Iguodala was to participate in the Semifinal game of the [[Basketball at the 2012 Summer Olympics – Men's tournament|2012 Summer Olympics]], during [[2012 United States men's Olympic basketball team|Team USA]]’s dominant victory over [[Argentina men's national basketball team|Argentina]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nbcphiladelphia.com/news/sports/iggy-dealt-while-representing-usa/2105652/?amp=1|title=Iggy Gets Dealt While Representing USA|date=August 10, 2012|work=nbcphiladelphia.com|publisher=NBC Philadelphia|access-date=October 14, 2025}}</ref> His arrival in Denver led to some league experts labeling Denver a contender.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/nuggets/news/denver-nuggets-acquire-all-star-olympian-andre-iguodala|title=Denver Nuggets acquire All-Star, Olympian Andre Iguodala|date=August 10, 2012|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc|access-date=August 11, 2012}}</ref> Iguodala returned on opening night of [[2012–13 Denver Nuggets season|2012–13]] to play his former team. Iguodala put up 11 points in an 84–75 loss, and received a mixed response from the crowd.<ref>{{cite news|last=Windhorst |first=Brian |title=Iguodala stumbles in return to Philly |date=October 31, 2012 |website=ESPN.com |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/8578747/andre-iguodala-return-philadelphia-rough-denver-nuggets-newcomer |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121104084807/http://espn.go.com/nba/story/_/id/8578747/andre-iguodala-return-philadelphia-rough-denver-nuggets-newcomer |archive-date=November 4, 2012 |url-status=live}}</ref> The Nuggets went on to make the playoffs with a franchise-record 57–25, and a team record 15 consecutive wins; however, they were upset in the first round by the [[Golden State Warriors]], despite Iguodala having a good series, averaging 18 points, 8.0 rebounds, 5.3 assists, and 2.0 steals per game in the series. This led to the firing of Nuggets coach [[George Karl]], who had just won the [[NBA Coach of the Year Award]].

====2014–15 season: First NBA championship and Finals MVP====
[[File:Andre Iguodala, Kris Humphries (16453091858).jpg|thumb|Iguodala fighting for the ball]]
Entering the [[2014–15 Golden State Warriors season|2014–15 season]], first-year Warriors coach [[Steve Kerr]] elected to move Iguodala from the starting rotation to the [[sixth man]] reserve position, in favor of forward [[Harrison Barnes]]. Since entering the NBA, Iguodala had played in 806 games as a starter without entering a game as a reserve, a league high over that span.<ref>{{cite web|last1=Dubow|first1=Josh|title=Iguodala's Willingness to Come off Bench Helps Key Warriors|url=https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/iguodalas-willingness-off-bench-helps-key-warriors-31582532|website=Associated Press|publisher=ABCNews.com|date=June 6, 2015|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150619021100/https://abcnews.go.com/Sports/wireStory/iguodalas-willingness-off-bench-helps-key-warriors-31582532|archive-date=June 19, 2015}}</ref> On March 18, 2015, he scored a then season-high 21 points on 9-of-12 shooting in a 114–95 win over the [[Atlanta Hawks]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150318/ATLGSW/gameinfo.html|title=Hawks at Warriors|website=nba.com|access-date=March 27, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20170925183132/http://www.nba.com/games/20150318/ATLGSW/gameinfo.html|archive-date=September 25, 2017|url-status=dead}}</ref> The Warriors advanced to the [[2015 NBA Finals]] to face the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]], where he was the team's best defender against Cavaliers star LeBron James. With Golden State down 2–1 in the series, Iguodala made his first start of the season, replacing [[Center (basketball)|center]] [[Andrew Bogut]] in Game 4. Iguodala scored a season-high 22 points on 8-of-15 shooting, which included four three-pointers. The Warriors' small lineup, which came to be known as the [[Death Lineup]], helped turn the series around.<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors at Cavaliers |website=nba.com|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150611/GSWCLE/gameinfo.html|access-date=March 27, 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|last=Holmes |first=Baxter |title=Iguodala NBA's no-stats Finals MVP? |date=June 16, 2015 |publisher=ESPN |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs/2015/story/_/id/13086040/andre-iguodala-game-finds-acceptance-warriors |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150617040403/http://espn.go.com/nba/playoffs/2015/story/_/id/13086040/andre-iguodala-game-finds-acceptance-warriors |archive-date=June 17, 2015 |url-status=live}}</ref> The Warriors defeated the Cavaliers in six games, and Iguodala was named the [[Bill Russell NBA Finals Most Valuable Player Award|Finals MVP]], becoming the first player to win the award without starting a game during the regular season.<ref>{{cite web|title=Warriors at Cavaliers|website=nba.com |url=http://www.nba.com/games/20150616/GSWCLE/gameinfo.html|access-date=March 27, 2018|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150617195310/http://www.nba.com/games/20150616/GSWCLE/gameinfo.html|archive-date=June 17, 2015|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.sfgate.com/warriors/article/Iguodala-Unlikely-Finals-MVP-6331753.php|title=Andre Iguodala: unlikely Finals MVP|website=sfgate.com|date=June 17, 2015|access-date=March 27, 2018}}</ref> He was also the first Finals MVP to not have started every game in the Finals.<ref name="Strauss">{{cite web |url=https://www.espn.com/nba/playoffs/2015/story/_/id/13096860/andre-iguodala-golden-state-warriors-named-nba-finals-mvp|title=Andre Iguodala named Finals MVP after coming off bench to begin series |website=[[ESPN]] |last=Strauss |first=Ethan Sherwood |date=June 16, 2015 |publisher=ESPN |access-date=March 27, 2018}}</ref> Iguodala finished the series averaging 16.3 points, 4.0 assists, and 5.8 rebounds. ====2015–16 season: Sixth Man of the Year runner-up====

In the second round, Iguodala helped the Warriors defeat the [[Portland Trail Blazers]] in five games to qualify for the Western Conference Finals. In their conference finals match-up with the [[Oklahoma City Thunder]], Iguodala helped the Warriors fight back from a 3–1 deficit in the series to win clinch a 4–3 victory. In Game 6 of the series, Iguodala's defense on [[Kevin Durant]] and [[Russell Westbrook]] was key to the Warriors forcing Game 7. In Game 7, Iguodala started in place of [[Harrison Barnes]] and again marked Kevin Durant. With a Game 7 victory, the Warriors moved on to the [[2016 NBA Finals|NBA Finals]] for the second straight year.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/nba/la-sp-warriors-cavaliers-finals-20160531-snap-story.html|title=With Andre Iguodala back in the starting lineup, Warriors are back in the NBA Finals|first=Ben|last=Bolch|website=[[Los Angeles Times]]|date=May 31, 2016|access-date=March 27, 2018}}</ref> The Warriors would again play the [[Cleveland Cavaliers]] for the championship. === Miami Heat (2020–2021) ===
====2019–20 season: Sixth NBA Finals appearance====
On July 7, 2019, Golden State traded Iguodala along with a protected first-round draft pick to the [[Memphis Grizzlies]] for [[Julian Washburn]]. The Warriors received a [[traded player exception]] in the deal.<ref name="warriors_07072019">{{Cite press release|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2019/07/07/warriors-trade-iguodala-will-retire-jersey-official-release|title=Warriors trade Andre Iguodala to Grizzlies; Lacob says team will retire jersey|date=July 7, 2019|publisher=Golden State Warriors|language=en|access-date=July 7, 2019}}</ref> Golden State was eyeing a replacement for Thompson while he recovered from his injury, and the trade freed [[NBA salary cap|salary cap]] space for them to acquire All-Star guard [[D'Angelo Russell]] in a sign-and-trade package with the [[Brooklyn Nets]] for Durant, who had announced earlier that he planned to sign with the Nets.<ref>{{cite news|last=Lowe|first=Zach|date=July 2, 2019|title=Why the collapse of the Warriors feels so abrupt|website=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/27100698/why-collapse-warriors-feels-abrupt|access-date=July 10, 2019}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|date=July 7, 2019|title=Warriors Acquire All-Star Guard D'Angelo Russell From Brooklyn Nets|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/warriors-acquire-russell-20190707|website=NBA.com}}</ref> Afterwards, the Warriors stated that they planned to eventually [[retired number|retire]] Iguodala's No. 9 jersey.<ref name="warriors_07072019" />

The Grizzlies, who were rebuilding, reached an agreement before training camp to allow Iguodala to stay away from the team and train on his own. They kept Iguodala on their 15-man opening day roster instead of buying out the 35-year-old veteran, who was earning $17 million in the last year of his contract.<ref>{{cite news|last=Cobb|first=David|date=November 29, 2019|title=Should the Blazers be a candidate to acquire Andre Iguodala from the Grizzlies?|newspaper=Memphis Commercial Appeal|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/2019/11/29/andre-iguodala-rumors-grizzlies-trade-candidate-blazers/4335972002/|access-date=January 15, 2020|via=USAToday.com}}</ref><ref name="cobb_10252019">{{cite news|last=Cobb|first=David|date=October 25, 2019|title=Analysis: Memphis Grizzlies betting on quality return for Andre Iguodala|newspaper=Memphis Commercial Appeal|url=https://www.usatoday.com/story/sports/nba/grizzlies/2019/10/25/andre-iguodala-trade-buyout-memphis-grizzlies-betting-good-return/4055185002/|access-date=January 15, 2020|via=USAToday.com}}</ref> Memphis was hoping for a quality trade with a playoff contender in exchange for Iguodala and his championship experience. Iguodala's decision to remain away from the team drew backlash from teammates, notably [[Dillon Brooks]] and [[Ja Morant]], who said his refusal to play was disrespectful.<ref name="cobb_10252019" /><ref>{{cite news|last=Sankofa|first=Omari II|date=September 16, 2019|title=The opportunity cost of trading Andre Iguodala — mapping out a decision timeline|work=The Athletic|url=https://www.nytimes.com/athletic/1214590/2019/09/16/the-opportunity-cost-of-trading-andre-iguodala-mapping-out-a-decision-timeline/|url-access=subscription|access-date=January 15, 2020}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|last=Shiller|first=Drew|date=February 4, 2020|title=Grizzlies' Ja Morant fires back as Steph Curry defends Andre Iguodala|url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/warriors/grizzlies-ja-morant-fires-back-steph-curry-defends-andre-iguodala|access-date=July 25, 2020|website=NBC Sports}}</ref>

On February 6, 2020, Iguodala was traded to the [[Miami Heat]] in a three-team trade along with [[Jae Crowder]] and [[Solomon Hill (basketball)|Solomon Hill]] with Memphis and Minnesota. As part of the trade, he agreed to a two-year, $30 million extension with Miami, with the last year being a team option.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/heat/news/heat-acquire-iguodala-crowder-hill-020620|title=Heat Acquire Andre Iguodala, Jae Crowder & Solomon Hill|website=NBA.com|date=February 6, 2020}}</ref> The Heat reached the [[2020 NBA Finals]], where they lost 4–2 to the [[Los Angeles Lakers]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Abrams|first=Jonathan|date=December 7, 2020 |url=https://www.nytimes.com/2020/12/07/sports/basketball/andre-iguodala-miami-heat.html|title=An N.B.A. Veteran Turns Wisdom Into Wins, On and Off the Court|newspaper=The New York Times|access-date=April 16, 2022 |orig-year=Updayed January August 6, 2021}}</ref> Iguodala became the tenth player in NBA history to make it to six straight Finals.<ref>{{cite web|last=Kelapire|first=Ryan|date=September 27, 2020 |url=https://www.azdesertswarm.com/basketball/2020/9/27/21459282/andre-iguodala-nba-finals-six-straight-streak-heat-celtics-lakers-arizona-wildcats-nba|title=Andre Iguodala joins elite company with sixth straight trip to NBA Finals|website=Arizona Desert Swarm|access-date=April 16, 2022}}</ref>

====2020–21 season: First-round exit====
Iguodala continued with the Heat in a bench-role in [[2020–21 Miami Heat season|2020–21]]. After the season, Miami did not exercise their $15 million option on his contract for the 2021–22 season, making Iguodala a free agent.<ref>{{Cite web|date=2021-08-01|title=Heat decline Iguodala option, pick up Dragic's|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/31936059/miami-heat-decline-andre-iguodala-option-pick-goran-dragics|access-date=2021-08-01|website=ESPN.com|language=en}}</ref>

===Return to Golden State (2021–2023)===
====2021–22 season: Fourth NBA championship====
On August 10, 2021, Iguodala returned to the [[Golden State Warriors]].<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/andre-iguodala-20210810|title=Warriors Sign 2015 NBA Finals MVP Andre Iguodala |work=NBA.com|date=August 10, 2021}}</ref> He missed 31 games from January to April with back soreness.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Warriors' Andre Iguodala: Available versus OKC |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/warriors-andre-iguodala-available-versus-okc/ |access-date=May 10, 2022 |website=CBS Sports|date=February 7, 2022 }}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |title=Warriors' Andre Iguodala: Available out of nowhere |url=https://www.cbssports.com/fantasy/basketball/news/warriors-andre-iguodala-available-out-of-nowhere/ |access-date=May 10, 2022 |website=CBS Sports|date=March 28, 2022 }}</ref> Iguodala went on to win his fourth championship after the Warriors defeated the [[Boston Celtics]] in six games of the [[2022 NBA Finals]], in limited playing time.

====2022–23 season: Final season====
On September 23, 2022, Iguodala re-signed with the Warriors on a one-year, fully guaranteed, $2.9 million contract (the veteran's minimum) and announced his decision to retire after the season.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/story/_/id/34650462/golden-state-warriors-forward-andre-iguodala-returning-19th-nba-season|title=Golden State Warriors veteran forward Andre Iguodala returning for 19th NBA season|access-date=September 23, 2022|website=[[ESPN]]|date=September 23, 2022 }}</ref>

After missing the first 39 games due to a hip injury, Iguodala made his season debut on January 8, 2023, in a 115–101 loss to the [[Orlando Magic]].<ref>{{Cite web |title=Andre Iguodala will make season debut vs. Magic; Andrew Wiggins to return to lineup on minutes restriction |url=https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/andre-iguodala-will-make-season-debut-vs-magic-andrew-wiggins-to-return-to-lineup-on-minutes-restriction/ |access-date=2023-01-08 |website=CBSSports.com |date=January 8, 2023 |language=en}}</ref> In just his eighth appearance, Iguodala fractured his left wrist against the [[Phoenix Suns]], requiring surgery.<ref>{{cite web |title=Tweet on Twitter |url=https://twitter.com/warriors/status/1636140391966834689}}</ref>

=== Retirement ===
On October 20, 2023, Iguodala announced his retirement after 19 seasons in the NBA.<ref name=":1">{{cite web|title=Four-Time Champion Andre Iguodala Announces NBA Retirement|url=https://www.nba.com/warriors/news/four-time-champion-andre-iguodala-announces-nba-retirement-20231020|work=NBA.com|date=October 20, 2023|access-date=October 20, 2023}}</ref> On February 23, 2025, the Golden State Warriors retired his No. 9 jersey in a ceremony at Chase Center, honoring Iguodala's significant contributions during his time with the team.<ref>{{Cite news |last=He |first=Eric |date=February 23, 2025 |title=Andre Iguodala has his number retired by the Warriors as a winner of an NBA Finals MVP and 4 titles |url=https://apnews.com/article/andre-iguodala-jersey-retirement-e6ee748e482e981667e406c2955176df |work=The Associated Press}}</ref>

==National team career==
[[Image:Linas Kleiza.jpg|thumb|right|Iguodala (left) strips the ball from [[Linas Kleiza]] as a member of Team USA.]]
Iguodala was a member of the [[United States men's national basketball team|U.S. national team]] in the [[2010 United States men's FIBA World Championship team|2010 FIBA World Championship]], winning the [[gold medal]]. There, he displayed his athleticism with an array of fastbreak dunks.

Iguodala was also selected for the [[2012 United States men's Olympic basketball team|2012 London Olympics team]], largely due to his exceptional defensive ability.<ref>{{cite web|last=Golliver |first=Ben |url= https://www.cbssports.com/nba/news/usa-basketball-finalizes-2012-london-olympics-12-man-roster/ |title=USA Basketball finalizes 2012 London Olympics 12-man roster |publisher=CBSSports.com |date=July 7, 2012 |access-date=January 18, 2023}}</ref> He helped Team USA win the gold medal against [[Spain national basketball team|Spain]] in a 107–100 victory. Coach [[Mike Krzyzewski]] called Iguodala one of the team's best players, and compared his game to that of [[Scottie Pippen]].<ref name="New Pippen">{{cite news|last=Abrams|first=Jonathan|title=The New Pippen|url=http://www.grantland.com/story/_/id/10041396/how-andre-iguodala-scottie-pippen|access-date=December 11, 2013|newspaper=Grantland|date=December 11, 2013}}</ref>

Iguodala also won a bronze medal with the United States at the [[FIBA Americas Under-18 Championship]] in 2002.<ref>{{cite web |title=Andre Iguodala |date=June 1, 2014 |publisher=USA Basketball |url=http://archive.usab.com/bios/iguodala_andre.html |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140720202403/http://archive.usab.com/bios/iguodala_andre.html |archive-date=July 20, 2014 |url-status=dead |access-date=November 17, 2015}}</ref>

==Personal life==
In August 2015, Iguodala married his childhood sweetheart, Christina Gutierrez. They have two children.<ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.tmz.com/2016/01/06/andre-iguodala-court-child-support/|title=Andre Iguodala -- In Court for Baby Mama Showdown ... Where's My Money Going?|work=TMZ|access-date=September 22, 2017}}</ref><ref>{{Cite news|url=http://www.csnbayarea.com/warriors/iguodala-sheds-light-decision-return-warriors-he-started-crying|title=Iguodala sheds light on decision to return to Warriors: 'He started crying...'|date=July 2, 2017|work=NBCS Bay Area|access-date=September 22, 2017}}</ref> On June 25, 2019, Iguodala released ''The Sixth Man: A Memoir''.<ref name="d019">{{cite web |last=Murray |first=Patrick |date=2019-05-28 |title=Andre Iguodala On 'The Sixth Man,' Retirement And The Pressures Faced By The Modern Athlete |url=https://www.forbes.com/sites/patrickmurray/2019/05/28/andre-iguodala-on-the-sixth-man-retirement-and-the-pressures-faced-by-the-modern-athlete/ |access-date=2024-10-22 |website=Forbes}}</ref>

Iguodala is a [[Christianity|Christian]]. He has said, "Faith is something I heavily lean on to give me that balance. I make sure I stay in chapel and have a good relationship with our chaplain. It keeps me focused … When people see us on the court, we want them to see God's work. We want to be a good representation of what we believe in …When you go out there, you’re not just representing your country or the NBA, you’re representing your beliefs. ''[[The Sporting News]]'' named Iguodala one of "the good guys of 2006" for establishing the Andre Iguodala Disaster Relief Fund that raised money for tornado victims in his hometown of Springfield, Illinois.<ref name="iguodala1"/> He later established the Andre Iguodala Youth Foundation, whose stated mission is to use sports as a means to help youths. The organization has hosted basketball camps and the annual "Thanksgiving with Dre", which has distributed food baskets to families in need.<ref>{{cite news | title = Iguodala foundation assists families | newspaper = The State Journal-Register | url = http://www.sj-r.com/article/20101121/News/311219982/?Start=1 | date = November 21, 2010 | access-date = March 23, 2015 | first = Debra | last = Landis}}</ref>

Alongside teammate [[Stephen Curry]], Iguodala is known to be an avid golfer.<ref name="g382">{{cite web | title=Hooked: Golden State Warriors Star Andre Iguodala Has Become A Golf Fanatic | website=Golf Digest | date=2016-06-07 | url=https://www.golfdigest.com/story/golden-state-warriors-star-andre-iguodala-has-become-a-golf-fanatic | access-date=2025-01-24}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/article/2017/08/03/andre-iguodala-pga-championship-turner-sports|title=Andre Iguodala puts golf passion to work at PGA Championship|author=Jon Krawczynski|agency=Associated Press|website=NBA.com|language=en|access-date=August 6, 2017}}</ref> He enjoys playing video games, particularly the ''[[NBA 2K]]'' series. ==Media figure and business interests==
Iguodala is a [[high tech|tech]] investor and a leading advocate for athletes in the NBA to invest in the technology industry. His partnership with entrepreneurs in San Francisco's Silicon Valley has led to an annual event tagged Players Technology Summit. The inaugural edition of the event began in 2017 where Iguodala and teammate [[Stephen Curry]] played hosts.<ref name="auto">{{Cite web|url=http://basketballwithinborders.com/silicon-valley-warriors-andre-iguodala-blazing-the-trail-for-the-nba-in-players-technology-summit/|title=Silicon Valley Warrior: Andre Iguodala blazing the trail for the NBA in Players Tech Summit {{!}} BWB|website=basketballwithinborders.com|language=en-US|access-date=August 20, 2018}}</ref> The second edition saw other athletes from the NBA like [[Kevin Durant]] and [[Jaylen Brown]] make debuts. The Players Technology Summit, sponsored by Bloomberg, was established as a platform to set a discourse and help shape conversations for athletes' financial future through opportunities in the technology industry.<ref name="auto"/> At a launch event on June 3, 2023, Bay Area-based professional [[women's association football|women's soccer]] club [[Bay FC]] announced that Iguodala was a minority owner of the team.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Novy-Williams |first1=Eben |date=June 3, 2023 |title=NBA Champion Andre Iguodala Invests in New NWSL Club Bay FC |url=https://sports.yahoo.com/nba-champion-andre-iguodala-invests-213115562.html |access-date=June 4, 2023 |work=[[Sportico]] |publisher=[[Yahoo!]]}}</ref> Iguodala is also a minority shareholder in the [[Premier League]] soccer club [[Leeds United F.C.|Leeds United]].<ref>{{Cite web |date=2024-05-09 |title=Full list of Leeds key figures and 15 known investors after Will Ferrell takes stake |url=https://www.yorkshireeveningpost.co.uk/sport/football/leeds-united/full-list-of-leeds-united-key-figures-and-15-known-investors-after-will-ferrell-takes-stake-4621066 |access-date=2026-06-18 |website=Yorkshire Evening Post |language=en}}</ref>

Together with partner Rudy Cline-Thomas, Iguodala has been able to invest in companies like Facebook, Twitter, and Tesla. The two have also invested in at least 25 different [[startup]]s in the technology industry.<ref name="auto"/>

Iguodala is a Venture Partner in the Catalyst Fund, which invests in underrepresented founders and entrepreneurs of tech companies.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://hauteliving.com/2020/05/andre-iguodala-cover-story-haute-living-miami/686838/ |title=Andre Iguodala On Upping His Game From The Basketball Court To The Boardroom |date=20 May 2020 |access-date=28 September 2020 |work=[[Haute Living]] |author=Violet Camacho}}</ref>

In February 2019, Iguodala was elected first vice-president of the [[National Basketball Players Association]] (NBPA), succeeding [[LeBron James]]. Iguodala had previously served as vice-president of the NBPA executive committee starting in 2013.<ref>{{cite news |date=February 19, 2019 |title=Andre Iguodala voted first VP of National Basketball Players Association |url=https://www.nbcsports.com/bayarea/warriors/andre-iguodala-voted-first-vp-national-basketball-players-association |work=NBC Sports |language=en}}</ref> On November 9, 2023, the NBPA executive committee appointed him as NBPA Acting Executive Director.<ref name=":2" />

In May 2024, Iguodala was inducted into the [[Boys & Girls Clubs of America]] 2024 Alumni Hall of Fame class.<ref>{{cite web | title=Al Roker, Ronnie DeVoe, Andre Iguodala and More Inducted into Boys & Girls Clubs of America's Alumni Hall of Fame | date=May 27, 2024 | url=https://www.bgca.org/news-stories/2024/May/al-roker-ronnie-devoe-andre-iguodala-and-more-inducted-into-boys-girls-clubs-of-americas-alumni-hall-of-fame/ | work=bgca.org }}</ref><ref>{{cite news | title=Al Roker shares health update, talks getting inducted into Boys & Girls Club Hall of Fame | date=May 25, 2024 | url=https://www.11alive.com/video/life/al-roker-shares-health-update-talks-getting-inducted-into-boys-girls-club-hall-of-fame/85-29a3d071-1d6e-487d-aab7-f4e8a43ec6d8 | quote=Roker was among names such as Allen Iverson, Andre Iguodala and Damar Hamlin to be inducted. | work=11alive.com }}</ref>
